chunks: He said: Abul Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qawlawayh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrated to me, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa al-Yaqtini, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, said:

Once, when Musa ibn Imran, peace be upon him, was seated, Iblis approached him wearing a hooded cloak of various colours. When he drew near to Musa, he removed the cloak, came forward and greeted him. Musa said: 'Who are you?' He said: 'I am Iblis.' Musa said: 'May Allah not bring your abode near anyone! Why have you come?' He said: 'I have only come to greet you because of your status before Allah, Mighty and Majestic.' So Musa said to him: 'Then what is this cloak?' He said: 'With it I seize the hearts of the children of Adam.'

Musa said to him: 'Tell me about the sin which, when the son of Adam commits it, you overpower him.' He said: 'When he becomes conceited with himself, regards his good deeds as too many, and his sin seems small in his eyes.'

Then he said to him: 'I advise you with three counsels, O Musa! Do not be alone with a woman, and do not let her be alone with you, for no man is alone with a woman nor she with him except that I am his companion to the exclusion of my associates. And beware of making a covenant with Allah, for whenever anyone pledges a covenant with Allah, I am his companion to the exclusion of my associates until I come between him and its fulfillment. And when you intend to give charity, give it immediately, for when a servant intends to give charity, I am his companion to the exclusion of my associates, coming between him and it.'
Then Iblis turned away saying: 'O woe and grief! I have taught Musa what he will teach the children of Adam!'

key_terms.استحوذت: Istahwadhtu: to overpower or gain mastery over someone
key_terms.برنس: Burnus: a hooded cloak, symbolizing Iblis's disguise and tool of deception
key_terms.خصال: Khisal: traits or counsels, here three pieces of advice

ai.seo_question: What did Iblis teach Prophet Musa about his strategies against humans?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a remarkable encounter between Prophet Musa (Moses) and Iblis (Satan), transmitted through the Prophet Muhammad. Iblis reveals three critical strategies he uses to lead humans astray: he personally intervenes when men and women are alone together, when someone makes a covenant with God, and when someone intends to give charity. He also discloses that self-conceit, overestimating one's good deeds, and belittling one's sins are the conditions that give him power over a person.
